tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_fs_tree
tools.valence: The directory tree under an absolute path. Ground here before reading: every mode's paths (source · mountpoint · files) come from mode_find. Example: { path: "/home/operator/jdex", depth: 2 }.

path.description: Absolute path to a directory. Example: "/home/operator/jdex/20-29 company"

tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_fs_find
tools.valence: Files matching a regex over the file name, searched under an absolute path; answers absolute paths. Example: { pattern: "\\.md$", path: "/home/operator/jdex" }.

pattern.description: JavaScript regex matched against file names. Example: "\\.md$"

path.description: Absolute path to the directory to search. Example: "/home/operator/jdex/20-29 company"

tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_fs_read
tools.valence: Read a file at an absolute path. Long files come back cut at 16 kB with a note — pass range (line numbers, 1-based) for the rest. Example: { path: "/home/operator/jdex/README.md", range: { from: 40, to: 120 } }.

path.description: Absolute path to the file. Example: "/home/operator/jdex/20-29 company"

tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_fs_write
tools.valence: Write or append a file at an absolute path. Parent directories are created. Example: { path: "/home/operator/jdex/22 finance/22.04 notes.md", content: "# notes" }.

path.description: Absolute path to the file. Example: "/home/operator/jdex/20-29 company"

content.description: The whole text to write, or the text to append. Example: "# notes"

tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_fs_stat
tools.valence: Size, modification time and format of one file at an absolute path. Example: { path: "/home/operator/jdex/README.md" }.

path.description: Absolute path to the file. Example: "/home/operator/jdex/20-29 company"

tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_fs_move
tools.valence: Move or rename a file, both ends absolute; parent directories are created. Example: { from: "/home/operator/jdex/draft.md", to: "/home/operator/jdex/22 finance/22.04 draft.md" }.

from.description: Absolute path to the file as it is. Example: "/home/operator/jdex/20-29 company"

to.description: Absolute path to where it goes. Example: "/home/operator/jdex/20-29 company"

tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_fs_delete
tools.valence: Delete one file at an absolute path. Directories are refused. Example: { path: "/home/operator/jdex/draft.md" }.

path.description: Absolute path to the file. Example: "/home/operator/jdex/20-29 company"

tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_shell_run
tools.valence: One-shot shell command in an absolute working directory. The output tail and the exit code come back; a nonzero code is information, not failure. Example: { command: "ls | head", cwd: "/home/operator/jdex" }.

command.description: The command, run through the shell. Example: "ls | head"

tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_entity_schema
tools.valence: Ground yourself before querying. No arguments: every entity on this daemon with row counts and card fields — buffer, thread, turn, literal, symbol and whatever else it opened. With entity: its columns, relations, filter operators, repository extensions and the card projection. Returns { entities: [{ type, rows, card }] } without an argument, { schema: { entity, rows, columns, relations, operators, extensions, card } } with one. Example: { entity: "buffer" }

entity.description: Entity type from the no-argument listing. Example: "buffer"

tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_entity_find
tools.valence: Query any entity on this daemon — the buffers on a thread, a thread's turns, literals by slug. Rows come back as cards — the lean agent projection; fields full only when a card lacks something you need. Columns, operators and extensions via entity_schema. Page by passing next.offset back as offset. Returns { <entity>: [rows], total, next?: { offset } }. Example: { entity: "buffer", where: { thread: "01a09010-13aa-778b-bce7-19c38f835337" }, fields: "full" }

entity.description: Entity type — list them via entity_schema. Example: "buffer"

where.description: MikroORM filter over the entity's columns and relations; operators $eq $ne $in $nin $like $gt $gte $lt $lte $and $or $not. Example: { thread: "01a09010-13aa-778b-bce7-19c38f835337", status: { $in: ["PENDING", "ACTIVE"] } }

fields.description: card: the repository's lean projection (id, slug, traits unless it declares its own); full: every column. Example: "full"

offset.description: Rows to skip — pass next.offset back. Example: 12

tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_entity_count
tools.valence: Count matching rows without loading them — cheap grounding before a find. Returns { count }. Example: { entity: "buffer", where: { thread: "01a09010-13aa-778b-bce7-19c38f835337" } }

entity.description: Entity type — list them via entity_schema. Example: "buffer"

where.description: MikroORM filter, the same shape entity_find takes. Example: { thread: "01a09010-13aa-778b-bce7-19c38f835337" }

tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_entity_update
tools.valence: Write trait data on one entity of this daemon — a literal's translation, a buffer's label. Pass the entity type, a where naming the one entity, and a trait patch keyed by trait name; the patch merges deep over the held data, a new name joins its traits. Find the entity first via entity_find. Returns { message, <entity>: [the entity] }.

entity.description: Entity type — list them via entity_schema.

where.description: MikroORM filter naming the one entity, the shape entity_find takes.

trait.description: trait data by name, merged deep over what the entity holds

tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_buffer_update
tools.valence: Write a buffer — the shared working surface between you and the user. Pass the buffer id and a data patch; the patch merges over the existing data keys. For a content buffer pass `source` instead: the file it loads is rewritten, same row, new hash. This thread's id is in the runtime row of your context; its buffer ids come from entity_find { entity: "buffer", where: { thread } }, or from the thread section when your primer carries one. Returns { message, buffer: [{ id, index, status, mime, data, trait }] }. Example: { id: "01a09010-18e0-736f-ad3f-a65b44d3fa43", data: { summary: "Six species on four continents." } }

data.description: Data keys to merge over buffer.data; keys you omit stay. Example: { summary: "Six species on four continents." }

source.description:
New content for the file this buffer loads, whole. Example: "# Q3 · final

Revenue …"

tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_buffer_label
tools.valence: Name a buffer. The label is what the operator reads on the buffer's line in the chat and in the buffer list — set it when a buffer's subject is clearer than its name, or when the operator asks. Returns { message, buffer: [{ id, index, status, data, view, trait }] }. Example: { id: "01a0856f-425f-72b8-b36f-decc1bb2050e", label: { name: "Flamingo", description: "Six species, range and diet" } }

name.description: The short display name the operator reads on the line — a subject, not a sentence. Example: "Flamingo — six species"

description.description: One sentence on what the thing holds, for the tooltip and the list. Example: "Range, diet and the six species, from Wikipedia and two field guides."

tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_thread_update
tools.valence: Write a thread's trait data — its configuration surface. Pass the thread id and a trait patch keyed by trait name (e.g. MASKED query data); each named trait's data merges over the existing value. This thread's id is in the runtime row of your context. Returns { message, thread: [{ id, phase, traits, trait, counter }] }. Example: { id: "01a09010-13aa-778b-bce7-19c38f835337", trait: { LABELED: { name: "Q3 filings" } } }

trait.description: Trait data to merge, keyed by trait name. Example: { LABELED: { name: "Q3 filings", description: "the filings correspondence" } }

tools.name: runtime_harness_runtime_mode_find
tools.valence: Every mode of this daemon with its paths on disk — source, mountpoint, files — as rows: the absolute paths fs_* and shell_run take. The first row is the daemon and its mountpoint. Narrow by type or slug. Returns { message }. Example: { type: "office" }
